To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
unsaturated fatty acids inhibit ToxT DNA binding and virulence gene expression by interacting with ToxT monomer and not dimer.
UFAs directly inhibit ToxT activity, specifically by inhibiting monomeric Toxin binding to DNA.
unsaturated fatty acids directly reduce DNA binding by Toxin Coregulated Pilus (TCP) transcription factor ToxT, thereby decreasing transcription of the TCP and cholera toxin virulence genes.

the mechanism for the inhibition of virulence gene expression in Vibrio cholera, the causative agent of the severe diarrheagenic disease cholera.
